interest: Shows Japan's 1930s religious controls, from Christian surveillance to Islamic outreach, culminating in the 1939 Religious Organizations Law.
overview: Docket (1933-39) on Japan's religious policy: Shinto-as-religion debates, Christian surveillance, Cardinal Dougherty's imperial audience, Islamic outreach (the Tokyo Mosque), and the 1939 Religious Organizations Law.

people.name: George S. McCune
people.role: President, Union Christian College of Korea

people.name: William F. Quillian
people.role: General Secretary, General Board of Christian Education, Methodist Episcopal Church, South

people.name: Koki Hirota
people.role: Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan

people.name: Eugene H. Dooman
people.role: Counselor of Embassy / Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits a letter introducing Mr. H. Hirayama traveling to the United States to arrange the purchase and distribution of his motion picture depicting the persecution of Japanese Christians.
subfiles.from: Union Christian College of Korea (George S. McCune)
subfiles.summary: McCune introduces Hirayama, touring the US to sell his film on Japan's 'Twenty Six Martyrs' Christian persecution.
subfiles.title: Letter from George S. McCune introducing H. Hirayama and 'The Twenty Six Martyrs of Japan' film

subfiles.about: Acknowledges correspondence regarding Hirayama's film and notes handling through diplomatic channels and the Japanese information office.
subfiles.summary: Grew acknowledges liaison on a Japanese film about early Christian martyrs, handled through regular diplomatic channels.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 62 from Grew regarding diplomatic handling of Japanese cinema mission

subfiles.about: Reports on the Home Ministry Commission's three-year inquiry into whether Shrine Shinto constitutes a religion and its inability to reach a unanimous decision.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: a Home Ministry commission spent three years undecided on whether Shrine Shinto counts as a religion, suspending its inquiry.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on Home Ministry Commission inquiry into State Shinto

subfiles.about: Transmits newspaper clippings from Yokohama reporting on the doctrines and activities of the Tenrikyo religion.
subfiles.summary: Consul Boyce forwards 1934 press clippings on the Tenrikyo religious sect.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on consular report and press clippings concerning Tenrikyo

subfiles.about: Requests a formal message of greeting from the Department of State or President Roosevelt for the Methodist General Conference in Japan.
subfiles.from: William F. Quillian (Methodist Episcopal Church, South)
subfiles.summary: Quillian asks whether State or FDR would send a goodwill message to Japan's 1935 Methodist General Conference.
subfiles.title: Letter from William F. Quillian requesting goodwill message for Methodist General Conference in Japan

subfiles.about: Declines to issue or recommend a presidential message of greeting to the Methodist conference in Japan in accordance with diplomatic usage.
subfiles.summary: State declines to send a goodwill message to Japan's Methodist conference, citing diplomatic custom.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State declining goodwill message for Methodist conference

subfiles.about: Quotes foreign press coverage reporting on Muslim activities and the status of Islam in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Minister Hornibrook relays a Tehran news article on the Muslim community in Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on Despatch No. 486 from Teheran regarding Muslims in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports that a Beirut organization designated an Islamic scholar to travel to Japan at their expense to teach Islam.
subfiles.summary: Beirut reports a Masonic Free-Thinkers group sent a Muslim scholar to Japan at its own expense to teach Islam.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on consular report from Beirut regarding Islamic mission to Japan

subfiles.about: Reports on Cardinal Dougherty's reception by Japanese church leaders and his private audiences with Emperor Hirohito and the Apostolic Delegate.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Cardinal Dougherty received separate formal audiences with Japanese church officials and Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on Despatch No. 2276 from Tokyo regarding Cardinal Dougherty's audience with the Emperor

subfiles.about: Transmits a missionary paper analyzing the relations between Christianity, Christian education, and the Japanese state.
subfiles.summary: A missionary's 1936 paper, forwarded via the International Missionary Council, examines state pressure on Christian schools in Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on International Missionary Council paper on Christianity and the state in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports on an official Japanese questionnaire circulated to twenty-four Christian organizations inquiring into their doctrines and beliefs.
subfiles.summary: Consul Makinson reports Japanese authorities sent a doctrinal questionnaire to twenty-four Christian organizations in Osaka.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on Despatch from Osaka regarding Japanese official questionnaire to Christian bodies

subfiles.about: Reports on the dedication of Tokyo's first mosque and Japan's strategic cultivation of Islamic leaders as an anti-communist measure.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the May 1938 dedication of Tokyo's first mosque, part of Japan's courting of Islam against Communism, amid rumored Italian funding and a Turkish boycott.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3036 from Grew on dedication of the Tokyo Mosque and Japanese Islamic policy

subfiles.about: Communicates with the Department of State regarding religious matters and missionary work in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Evangelist Dunlop writes to State about tightening Japanese controls on Christian evangelism.
subfiles.title: Letter from H. Parker Dunlop regarding religious matters in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports on proposed Japanese legislation designed to define the legal status of religious organizations and place them under state control.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards analysis of a proposed Japanese law to define and regulate all religious organizations' legal status.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3722 from Grew on proposed Religious Organizations Law

subfiles.about: Protests alleged discrimination against the Islamic faith in proceedings of the 74th Japanese Imperial Diet.
subfiles.summary: Glick protests to State over Diet discrimination against Islam, enclosing a formal resolution.
subfiles.title: Letter from L. Selim Glick protesting Diet discrimination against Islam

subfiles.about: Transmits an English translation and analysis of the newly promulgated Religious Organizations Law (Law No. 77).
subfiles.summary: Dooman reports the April 1939 promulgation of Japan's Religious Organizations Law, enclosing an English translation and analysis.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3910 from Dooman transmitting the Religious Organizations Law (Law No. 77)

subfiles.about: Summarizes the key regulatory mechanisms and provisions of Japan's newly enacted Religious Organizations Law.
subfiles.summary: Military Attaché report details the Religious Organizations Law's provisions as part of Japan's total national mobilization.
subfiles.title: Report No. 9819 from Military Attaché summarizing principal provisions of the Religious Organizations Law

subfiles.about: Reports on instances of persecution and harassment of Christian missionary workers by Japanese authorities in occupied China.
subfiles.summary: Consul Smyth documents 1939 persecution of Christian workers in Japanese-occupied China, citing missionary and consular reports.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet on Despatch No. 2151 from Smyth on persecution of Christian workers in China
